name: The Ascent and the Descent
_what: Info film for the Angelic and Demonic domain: the Seraphic Orders (Choir-Height) and the Abyssal Choir (the Bargain Gate and the Maw), per films/BRIEF.md.

lines: The old books called the two sides angels and demons.
Two peoples stand at those ends now: one goes up, one goes down.
The Abyssals draw on the far side directly, being the other half of the same argument.
The Seraphic Orders are human. Ordered nanite has made them radiant, and they bleed gold.
after: They take wild nanite and put it in order.

lines: Choir-Height: white spires in stepped rings, gold light from the high arches, and a choral certainty that is hard to bear.
Arrivals come in at the foot, in Choirfoot, where the sisters watch who flinches.
after: You may go up. You will be looked at first.

lines: A Seraph sees what a person has done and what they still carry, and lifts it, or pronounces on it.
Mercy House keeps its doors open. A Seraph who lifts a weight carries it after. The house is full of them, still standing.
Almost nothing runs unbroken from the world before the Transition. The Orders do.
Most judge and charter. A few, the Vessel-Keepers, keep the long-lived going.
Hierarch Brightmantle governs from Choir-Height. Her mercy costs her, and it shows at the eyes.
after: She knows what each Seraph has left to give.

lines: Inside the Orders an inquisition gains ground: a higher law with no mercy under it.
Some pronounce the Sentence: judgment on someone who never agreed to be weighed, binding whether or not it is true.
Higher still burn the Unfallen, who hold that mercy without judgment is complicity.
after: Their walls are blackened on the facing sides.

lines: They weigh anyone, at any distance, without their knowing.
A judgment that binds cannot be taken back. A mercy given wrongly is still given.
Across the world stands the Bargain Gate: horned gables, dark stone, stone tables set out in the open.
The Abyssal Choir names what you actually want, and its true price. Both sides pay.
after: The bargains are perfectly fair. That is the horror.

lines: On the Asking Floor every price is written on the wall a yard high.
after: Armies are offered terms. Most take them.

lines: In Appetite Halls the Choir says aloud the wants people cannot admit to.
after: Nobody is forgiven. Some call it the most liberating hour of their lives. Some never recover.

lines: Most of the Choir are traders. Others work the Hollow, naming a want the way a healer names a sickness.
Speaker Istvane hears every petition in public and sets terms that are always exactly fair.
after: Beside him is an empty chair he never looks at.

lines: Below, the Maw: a city built downward around a shaft, its lights fewer the deeper it goes.
after: The Devouring there have stopped bargaining, because a bargain implies a price.

lines: Anyone who says the abyss cannot compel has met only its traders.
after: The Maw prices a bargain against what cannot be refused: a child, a name, a breath.

lines: A bargain catches only someone who already wanted it. And what the abyss eats does not come back.
The Ascent weighs what you have done. The Descent names what you want.
after: Only one of them offers you a deal.

lines: Below the Ascent, at Stair Hollow, you can bring a case, lose, and go home.
Short of the Maw, at Lowmarket, everything is for sale and the price is on it.
Each Reach is leaning harder into its own extreme. At the top the walls scorch. At the bottom the lights thin.
One will weigh you. One will name what you want. Neither waits to be asked.

title.line2: The Seraphic Orders and the Abyssal Choir
